title: Batch Virtuoso: Workload Signature Extraction and Continuous Batch Policy Annealer
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Build a continuous, workload-driven batch recommendation engine that proposes and safely applies batching + KV-caching configs per deployment slice. Unlike a static autotuner, the Batch Virtuoso produces compact workload signatures, evaluates candidate parameter policies offline and in shadow, and performs staged, metric-gated rollouts with deterministic rollback. The system should reduce per-token unit cost while respecting latency SLOs and minimizing customer-visible errors. Scope includes: signature extractor, heuristic policy generator, offline/online evaluation harness, control-plane safe-apply primitives, telemetry alerts and runbook integration.
acceptance_criteria: Signature extractor produces a 128-byte canonical workload fingerprint for a given API route and timeframe
Policy generator yields candidate configs (batch_size, max_latency_budget_ms, kv_ttl_ms, prefix_cache_threshold) and ranks them by expected cost savings and risk score
Shadow evaluation framework can run candidate configs at 10% traffic in shadow with zero customer impact and produce the full metric delta set
Safe-apply implements a 3-phase rollout: shadow -> canary (1%) -> ramp (up to target) with automatic rollback on SLO violations
Automated rollback triggers on p95 latency regressions > 15% or error-rate increase > 2x baseline within 10 minutes
End-to-end integration test and e2e perf benchmark demonstrate >= 8% median cost reduction across sampled workloads without breaking SLOs

testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for fingerprint determinism and invariants; 2) Synthetic replay harness that replays production traces and applies candidate configs in shadow; 3) Staging A/B where canary is applied to a small subset of routes for 48 hours; 4) Chaos microburst tests that inject RPS spikes while measuring p95/p99.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: shadow-only (no traffic changes). Phase 1: canary 0.5% of traffic for 30 minutes. Phase 2: ramp to 5% for 2 hours, evaluate; Phase 3: ramp to target over 6 hours. Each phase gated by metric checks (see telemetry_signals). Manual approval required before Phase 3 for enterprise customers.
rollback_plan: All safe-apply operations store prev_effective_config and decision_log. Rollback is deterministic: immediate revert to prev_effective_config when circuit-breaker fires. Automated rollback criteria: p95_latency_ms > baseline_p95 * 1.15 OR error_rate > baseline_error_rate * 2 OR kv_hit_rate drop > 20 percentage points. Post-rollback: capture debugging traces and open follow-up ticket for analysis.
notes: Heuristic ideas to explore: multi-armed bandit for batch_size selection (Thompson sampling with safety priors), TTL-aware kv-tiling vs prefix-only caching, conditional batching where batch size scales with observed inter-request gap, and a conservative fallback library of pre-validated profiles for regulated customers.
